Criterion acceptance-public-surfaces (as accepted): Given an implementer adding tests, When any change adds a test, Then the test drives the app's CLI, HTTP or UI and calls no internal function or module directly.
Kind: weakens
What: acceptance-public-surfaces allows an integration test to drive a public library function besides the CLI, HTTP or UI.
Why: Owner rule after the pilot 1 run (Tom, 2026-10-20, PR #54): integration tests may enter through a public library function, e.g. pilot 1's build_context(); end-to-end tests and just qc still go through the CLI, HTTP or UI. ADR 0002 was rewritten in place and the spec followed it (owner yes: Tom, 2026-10-20).
Evidence: Pilot 1 run: a target whose public surface is a library function could not be integration-tested under 'the test drives the app's CLI, HTTP or UI and calls no internal function', which contradicted rewritten ADR 0002.

ADR 0002 was rewritten in place and the spec followed it (owner yes: Tom, 2026-10-20).

Criterion acceptance-signed-in (as accepted): Given the owner signed in to exe.dev, When the owner opens a spec's review link, Then the spec loads with its review controls, including Accept spec.
Kind: clarifies
What: review-accepted: the acceptance record is the review page's Accept hand-off for the spec at the registered commit, read by octo-feather-accepted from every session's registry rows and their spools.
Why: Nothing writes the registry's accepted registration the spec named, so the owner's Accept was never recorded (PR #56, owner approved 2026-10-20).
Evidence: Pilot 1 (2026-10-20): Tom pressed Accept spec, the page wrote its hand-off, and octo-feather-accepted still exited 1 waiting for a registry accepted = true that nothing writes; the agent hand-wrote it twice.

Criterion acceptance-fresh-green (as accepted): Given the owner with a new repository from either template, When the owner runs its gate, Then the gate passes and reports lint, types, structure and tests each as checked.
Kind: clarifies
What: templates-integrate-rule: only a repository created from a template has just integrate; a repository the kit did not create gains no factory recipe, agents run octo-feather-integrate and octo-feather-qc directly.
Why: Hand-in repos must stay clean (PR #56, owner approved 2026-10-20); ADR 0017 was rewritten in place to match.
Evidence: Pilot 1 (2026-10-20): the hand-in repo gained integrate/qc recipes in its justfile because the spec said every target defines them.

Criterion acceptance-prompt-eval (as accepted): Given a maintainer, When any change alters agent behavior by editing a prompt, a role file's contract, or a vendored-skill patch, Then it ships a recorded live smoke run of the changed behavior in evidence/, and the eval case it owes, one that fails before the change and passes after it, is listed as owed in docs/future.md until just qa runs it.
Kind: clarifies
What: An owed eval is listed in its own file under docs/owed-evals/ instead of docs/future.md; the criterion's requirement (a smoke in evidence/ and a listed owed eval until just qa runs it) is unchanged.
Why: Owner, issue #80 (finding 50): every lane appending to docs/future.md made nearly every pair of open PRs conflict there (#49/#73, #49/#78, #73/#78, #27/#35, #27/#31). ADR 0008 and check-behavior-smoke move to docs/owed-evals/ in the same PR; the spec follows.
Evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: docs/adr/0008-prose-last.md (corrected in place, issue #80) and scripts/check-behavior-smoke require a docs/owed-evals/*.md change, while quality#acceptance-prompt-eval and #quality-prompt-smoke said docs/future.md.

Criterion acceptance-lane-no-tickets (as accepted): Given a supervisor delivering several tickets, When a ticket changes state, then the director opens that ticket on GitHub, Then GitHub shows the ticket's new state, and the lane record holds no ticket entry.
Kind: adds
What: Tickets live in the target's tracker, not GitHub Issues only; the lane record's issue key holds the lane key.
Why: Owner ruling (2026-10-22, issue #82): the kit works with Linear directly so it can run on a Linear-first repository; the tracker is set per target in .octo-feather.toml, tracker work lives in packaged skills (github-pr, github-issues, linear) behind fixed script names, and ADR 0004 and 0011 were corrected in place to match.
Evidence: Corrected ADR 0004 says the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear, chosen per target, and ADR 0011 that a Linear lane's key is its lowercased ticket key, while the spec as accepted says 'tickets live in GitHub Issues only' (octo-lane-record-tickets); the accepted criteria cannot pass on a Linear target.

Criterion acceptance-kickoff-refuses (as accepted): Given the owner with a spec that has not been accepted, When the owner tells the director to build it, Then the director tells the owner the spec is not accepted and why, and GitHub shows no new parent issue and Herdr no lane workspace or supervisor tab for it.
Criterion acceptance-kickoff-lanes (as accepted): Given the owner with an accepted spec, When the owner merges its spec pull request, Then GitHub shows one new parent issue per lane the director cut, and Herdr shows one lane workspace per parent issue holding its supervisor.
Criterion acceptance-merge-approved-head (as accepted): Given the owner who said merge to a lane's merge ask, with the lane branch unchanged since the merge ask, When the director relays that merge to the lane's supervisor, Then GitHub shows the lane's pull request merged by the supervisor at the head the merge ask named, and its parent issue closed.
Criterion acceptance-repeat-lane (as accepted): Given a finding class that code review has logged twice across lanes, When the director checks finding classes after the next merge ask, Then GitHub shows a new parent issue for a correction lane naming that class, Herdr shows its workspace with one corrector, and every product lane keeps running.
Criterion acceptance-gate-correction-lane (as accepted): Given the owner who corrects an agent's work at a merge gate, When the director handles that correction, Then GitHub shows a new correction lane's parent issue quoting the owner's correction.

Criterion acceptance-one-head (as accepted): Given a lane ready for its merge ask, When the owner reads the merge ask, Then the head it names is the one just qc left, its last commit changes only the status file, the qc report named every criterion the lane builds, and the code review verdict names that same head.
Criterion acceptance-pilot-pr (as accepted): Given a supervisor whose pilot ticket was just integrated, When it sends the pilot's results up, then the owner opens the lane's draft pull request, Then the pull request exists, its status file marks the pilot's passed criteria built with that pull request's number in a status-only commit, and the pilot's review verdict names the head that commit made.
Criterion acceptance-qc-interim (as accepted): Given an integrated lane head whose lane builds three criteria, When the supervisor runs just qc naming all three and one fails, Then the qc report shows one pass or fail per named criterion, each with the command run and its output, from a code reviewer started fresh and headless for that run, and the new head's only change is the status file, marking the two passed criteria built and the failed one planned.
Kind: weakens
What: just qc and the code review run in parallel on the same integrated head H; the review verdict names H, not the qc status head H'; the merge ask names H' and both verdicts, and a check proves H to H' changes only the status files. A clean merge of main keeps the qc verdict when a check proves the lane's own diff is unchanged; the merge ask names the judged head, the refreshed head and the proof. The judge is a qc judge with its own role, not a code reviewer. Project rule renamed 'Review and qc judge one head'.
Why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1, 9 and 10 (Tom, 2026-10-21): QC is every check on what ships; the code reviewer does code quality only; qc and review must not wait on each other, and a clean main refresh must not rerun the judge. Marked weakens because the review verdict no longer names the exact merge head; the status-only check carries that guarantee instead.
Evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: docs/adr/0022 (corrected in place, issue #67 item 9: integrate, then qc and review in parallel, then the merge ask) and agents/qc-judge.md (the judge's own role, item 1) against issue-lifecycle#lanes-one-head 'its status-only commit is the head the fresh code review then judges' and #acceptance-qc-interim 'from a code reviewer started fresh'.

Criterion acceptance-qc-listed (as accepted): Given a supervisor with a final head the code reviewer passed, When the owner reads the merge ask, Then it shows the product judge's verdict for that head, per acceptance criterion.
Kind: clarifies
What: Code review runs in parallel with just qc on the same head; just qc's judge is a qc judge from its own role; the code reviewer judges code quality only and blocks only on a documented standards breach or a named simplification.
Why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1, 2 and 9.
Evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: docs/adr/0022 (corrected in place, issue #67 item 9) and agents/qc-judge.md against quality#qaqc-when 'then code review of the head qc left' and #recipe-qc 'a fresh code reviewer run headless'.

Criterion acceptance-tab-headless-same (as accepted): Given a maintainer, When a code reviewer is started in a worker tab, then one is run headless on the same head, Then both reviewers report the same model, thinking level, tools and skills, and both have loaded the target repository's AGENTS.md.
Kind: clarifies
What: The qc judge gets its own row and role file (agents/qc-judge.md); the code reviewer is no longer run headless for just qc, judges code quality only, reads pstack interrogate's code-quality review and lead-judgment references, and blocks only on a documented standards breach or a named simplification listing the lines it deletes.
Why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1 and 2: on #51 the reviewer built hostile setups from its 'run the changed behavior' line and the patch's broken-behaviour block; only 1 of 6 blocks traced to the spec. Fix by deleting those instructions.
Evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: agents/code-reviewer.md and .skillfile/patches/skills/code-review (issue #67 items 2 and 4 delete the Spec axis and the broken-behaviour block) against roles#roles-reviewer-patch 'it blocks only on a failed acceptance criterion, broken behavior or a hard standard' and #role-code-reviewer 'headless for each just qc run'.

Why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 2 to 5.
Evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: Skillfile and agents/*.md skills lines (issue #67 items 2, 3 and 5) against skills#skill-blast-radius 'loaded by code reviewer' and #loading-pstack 'leaves out interrogate'.

Criterion acceptance-patch-only (as accepted): Given a maintainer, When any change edits the text of a vendored skill, Then the edit lands as a patch in the skill's patch folder whose first line names the ADR it serves, and re-applying the pinned upstream with its patches reproduces the committed skill.
Kind: clarifies
What: The kit vendors the whole interrogate skill folder, patched to drop its Claude model row and fallback; no role loads it, and the code reviewer reads only its code-quality review and lead-judgment references.
Why: Issue #67 item 2 pins the two references via Skillfile; skillfile vendors skill folders only, so the folder comes with them.
Evidence: skillfile v1.9.2 skips a source path without SKILL.md ('source missing'), so references/ alone cannot be pinned; the earlier gh67 skills call said 'from interrogate only its code-quality review and lead-judgment references', contradicting the committed .agents/skills/interrogate/ folder and its patch .skillfile/patches/skills/interrogate/SKILL.md.patch.

Criterion acceptance-only-listed (as accepted): Given a supervisor in a target repository that has its own skills folder, When it starts an implementer there, Then the implementer has exactly the skills its role file lists available, and none from the target's folder or the kit's by discovery.
Kind: clarifies
What: blast-radius keeps a one-line patch dropping upstream's disable-model-invocation, reason 'ADR 0012 model-invoked: the implementer runs it', instead of no patch.
Why: Issue #67 item 3 moves blast-radius to the implementer's skills line; item 4 drops its patch. Without the patch Pi hides the skill from the implementer, so item 3 cannot hold. The patch is pruned to the one line #vendored-model-invoked already requires.
Evidence: Probe (gh87, no model call, system prompt dumped at before_agent_start): pi --no-skills --skill <upstream blast-radius, disable-model-invocation: true> --skill tdd lists only tdd in available_skills; Pi source visibleSkills = skills.filter(s => !s.disableModelInvocation). The gh67 call making skills#skill-blast-radius patch 'none' contradicts skills#acceptance-only-listed (the implementer has exactly the skills its role lists).

Criterion acceptance-patch-only (as accepted): Given a maintainer, When any change edits the text of a vendored skill, Then the edit lands as a patch in the skill's patch folder whose first line names the ADR it serves, and re-applying the pinned upstream with its patches reproduces the committed skill.
Kind: clarifies
What: writing-for-agents carries a patch removing its CLAUDE.md mentions, reason 'ADR 0001 Pi only', instead of no patch.
Why: Issue #67 item 5 vendors writing-for-agents; the kit's gate refuses Claude references outside docs (ADR 0001), as for interrogate.
Evidence: just check red on check-refs after vendoring upstream writing-for-agents: SKILL.md l3 'modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md' and l6 'an AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md' ('Claude/Codex references above; Pi is the only runtime (docs/adr/0001)'), contradicting the gh67 call giving skills#skill-writing-for-agents patch 'none'.

Criterion acceptance-tracker-default (as accepted): (not in the accepted spec)
Kind: clarifies

Evidence: skills tracker-role-line said 'pi-role loads the target's tracker skill in its place, with linear-cli beside linear', while interrogate (skill-interrogate-refs) is vendored and loaded by no role with its references read by path: two mechanisms for the same kind of upstream reference.

Criterion acceptance-tracker-scripts (as accepted): Given a maintainer, When any change leaves a tracker skill without one of the tracker scripts, Then the gate fails naming the skill and the missing script.
Kind: clarifies
What: issue-view's JSON also lists the keys of the ticket's sub-issues, so a general script reads a lane parent's tickets through the tracker skill.
Why: octo-feather-lane tickets PARENT (the to-tickets publish check of every lane's tickets) lists the parent's sub-issues; with issue-view as accepted it could only do so with its own gh issue view --json subIssues call, which is tracker-specific code in a general script, and has no Linear path.
Evidence: skills#boundary-tracker-skills: 'The kit's general scripts call the tracker scripts and hold no tracker-specific code' contradicts skills#tracker-script-issue-view printing no sub-issue keys, given scripts/octo-feather-lane line 984 reads `gh issue view PARENT --json number,subIssues` to list a lane's tickets.
